name: Boaz
bio:
Boaz is a wealthy and respected landowner in Bethlehem, a relative of Naomi's late husband Elimelech, who becomes Ruth's husband and family redeemer. He first appears watching over his harvest, greeting his workers with "The LORD be with you" — a small detail that marks him as a man of genuine faith rather than mere wealth. When he learns that the young Moabite woman gleaning in his field is Ruth, he already knows of her loyalty to Naomi, and he instructs his workers to let her glean freely and even leave extra grain for her — generosity that goes well beyond what the law of gleaning required.

When Ruth approaches him at the threshing floor asking him to act as her kinsman-redeemer, Boaz responds with honor rather than taking advantage of the vulnerable situation: he commends her for not pursuing a younger man, protects her reputation by sending her home before light, and moves immediately and publicly to settle the matter of redemption. At the town gate, he follows proper legal process, allowing a nearer kinsman the first right to redeem Elimelech's land and family line, and only steps in himself once that kinsman declines. By marrying Ruth, Boaz not only provides for two widows but becomes part of the family line leading to King David and, ultimately, to Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:5). Boaz is remembered as a model of integrity, generosity, and covenant faithfulness acted out in ordinary daily life.
